chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ismail ibn Mihran from Dorust ibn Abu Mansur from Ibn Muskan from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed, the souls are in the form of bodies in a tree in Paradise, recognizing each other and asking about one another. So when the soul arrives among the souls, they say, 'Leave it alone, for it has escaped from a great terror.' Then they ask it, 'What happened to so-and-so? And what happened to so-and-so?' If it says to them, 'I left him alive,' they hope for him; and if it says to them, 'He has perished,' they say, 'He has perished! Perished!'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition of souls in Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the Shia concept of 'Jasad al-Barzakh' (the subtle body), illustrating how souls retain a form analogous to their physical bodies while dwelling in a specific tree in Paradise. It underscores the continued social consciousness of the deceased, who actively inquire about the status of their loved ones, reflecting the interconnectedness of the spiritual community beyond death. This tradition is often cited by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid to support the tangible reality of the Barzakh realm.
